ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The graph shows a horizontal segment at y = -2 from about x = -5 to x = -2, with a filled point at x = -2. Separately, there is an open circle at (-2, 4) starting a curved branch. The curved branch descends and has an open circle at (1, -4), then continues upward to meet a line segment at about (3, 0). The line segment continues to a filled point near (5, 2). Reasoning: The graph already forces a discontinuity at x = -2, since f(-2) = -2 from the filled point, but the right-hand limiting value from the curve is 4. The problem says f is discontinuous for only one x-value in (-5, 5). Therefore the open circle at (1, -4) cannot represent another discontinuity. To make f continuous at x = 1, f(1) must equal the limit of the curve there, which is -4.

method.method_draft: Use a contradiction-style route. From the image, note that the graph has an unavoidable break at x = -2: the left piece gives the filled function value y = -2, while the curved piece approaches the open point y = 4 from the right.
